newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end mostly higher.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end mostly higher.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures ended mostly higher Thursday, with gold, silver and even platinum recovering some ground and only palladium ending lower after confirmation Russian metal exports to Japan resumed after a six-month suspension.

"Gold and silver saw a little more shortcovering, but with central bank activity still hanging over the gold market, there's not much fundamentally for the market to stand on, so prices may still go lower, though probably not that much lower from here," said Scott Meyers, analyst with Pioneer Futures in New York.
COMEX August gold ended up $1.90 at $320.80 an ounce after gapping higher on the open and then consolidating for most of the day. The August/December spread ended steady around $3.60.
Estimated total COMEX gold volume was 36,000 lots, considerably lower than the daily volume earlier this week.
The expiry of COMEX August gold options Friday was not expected to have much influence, as the market had moved down sharply away from the more active strike prices, traders said.
In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted at $319.60/$320.10 at the close compared to the London Thursday afternoon fix of $319.80 and the New York close Wednesday of $318.00/50.
Gold fixed at a 12-year low early Wednesday of $315.75 in London in the wake of last week's decision of Australian central bank to sell 167 tonnes of gold.
"The fall in the gold price is going to put quite a lot of strain on jobs at gold mines, possibly a few hundred thousand jobs are at stake," said a senior New York bullion banker.

"But I wouldn't be surprised to see recent price support levels around $316-317 an ounce attacked again, as we're unlikely to see the Mid East physical buying of earlier this week again until the price dips back to around $316," he said.

"Meanwhile, COMEX gold open interest could go higher still because a lot more gold has been lent by central banks into market to finance shorts in recent times, and OTC activity has been very active with a lot of borrowing going on," he added.
COMEX gold open interest rose a further 788 lots Wednesday to 218,754 contracts, its highest level in 18 months.
Implied gold lease rates were little changed but remained over 2.00 percent in most maturity months.

Further evidence of the trend toward more central bank mobilization of gold reserves was provided Thursday by news the Belgian parliament approved a bill to raise the amount of gold the Belgian central bank can sell in the form of bullion commemorative coins to a total of 133 tonnes.
Currently, Belgian law allows the central bank to sell up to a total of 36 tonnes of gold in the form of coins, and so far the bank has used about 26 tonnes of that facility.
Future coin sales would be limited to about 26 tonnes a year though, and will need the approval of the proposed European Central Bank.
In total, the Belgian central bank has sold about 733 tonnes of gold in the past ten years.
COMEX September silver settled up 6.3 cents at $4.383 after a jump near the close after a breach of Wednesday's high of $4.345.
NYMEX October platinum closed $0.60 firmer at $381.70 while NYMEX September palladium lost a further $6.35 to $148.40.
Japanese trade houses reported overnight that some Russian palladium had arrived in Japan, but platinum was not due to arrive until next week.
"Palladium was lower partly on the Russian news, but also partly on a flush of tickets not executed Wednesday went palladium ended limit down," one NYMEX floor trader said.

"But this market has probably already anticipated the return of Russian metal, and trade houses are already on the bid, so it wouldn't surprise me if PGMs (platinum group metals) go higher from here."
Russian PGM exports had been suspended for six months. Russia supplies about 60 percent of the world's palladium and 20 percent of its platinum.
